## Highlights

- **Schedule automations with the repeat picker.** A schedule offers presets from every 15 minutes to monthly, **Custom times** and **Custom interval**, and lists its next three runs. Local times hold through daylight-saving changes, and **Missed runs** decides whether a time missed while Tale was unavailable runs late or is skipped (**Skip them**). A trigger's fixed input gives every run the same values, and **This run receives** shows what a run gets. See [Triggers](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/automations/triggers). [#4619](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4619)
- **Read and replay every automation run, step by step.** A failed run opens with a card that says where and why it failed, and **How to fix**; each step shows what it read, received and returned, and why it ran or was skipped. **Play** plays the run back on its canvas, **Run again** starts it again with the same or an edited input, **Retry from this step** runs the step you choose and the steps that depend on it again and reuses the other results, and **Compare** shows two runs side by side. See [Execution logs](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/automations/execution-logs). [#4647](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4647)
- **New automation steps.** `http.get` and `http.send` call any HTTPS API, with a stored credential or without one; a live send asks for an approval first, as every write does ([HTTP](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/automations/http), [#4735](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4735)). `knowledge.search` searches the organization's knowledge ([Knowledge search](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/automations/knowledge-search), [#4739](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4739)), `task.create` creates a task ([Add tasks](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/automations/add-tasks), [#4757](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4757)) and `notify.member` notifies members ([Notify members](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/automations/notify-members), [#4760](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4760)).
- **Let one automation write without approval.** On an automation's **General** tab, **Runs without approval** lists each write its latest version makes to an outside system, and an Owner or Admin can let that automation make one without asking. A rule of the approval policy that requires a person still wins, and each grant and withdrawal is recorded in the audit log. See [Approvals in workflows](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/automations/approvals-in-workflows). [#4763](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4763)
- **Models the organization serves.** The **Model** picker of an `llm` or `agent` step lists the models your connected providers serve; for a model typed in that none of them serves, **Problems** warns that a live run would fail at that step. **Change model** replaces a model in every `llm` step that names it, at once. See [Workflow editor](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/automations/editor). [#4761](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4761)
- **Start from a blank automation that runs.** **Blank (trigger + agent)** takes a name, a model, instructions, equipment and when the automation runs; **Deploy v1 now**, on by default, puts its first version live at once. [#4694](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4694)
- **Organization settings over MCP.** A coding agent connected to the MCP endpoint reads the organization's settings with `get_settings`, plans a change with `plan_settings` and makes it with `apply_settings`, with the role of the person whose API key it uses. See [Settings over MCP](https://docs.tale.dev/develop/mcp-settings). [#4685](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4685)
- **Faster under load.** Audited writes no longer wait for one another: the worker seals the audit chain in batches, within seconds ([#4700](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4700)). Each API process answers sessions and organization memberships from a cache, so ordinary requests skip those database reads ([#4703](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4703)). Automation code runs in a pool of runner processes ([#4693](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4693)).
- A connector's settings fields appear in the reader's language ([#4746](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4746)). Retained deployment observation is bound to the exact deployment reference before it reads runtime state, keeping recovery evidence tied to the operation it describes ([#4755](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4755)).

## Upgrade notes

- Deploy the Tale platform and the Tale CLI together. The backend applies 12 forward-only database migrations at boot: `0170_automation_schedule_rules.sql`, `0171_automation_trigger_skip_detail.sql`, `0172_automation_trigger_static_input.sql`, `0173_seeded_github_schedules_off.sql`, `0190_automation_node_runs.sql`, `0191_automation_run_replays.sql`, `0192_automation_run_replay_lineage.sql`, `0193_boot_repairs.sql`, `0194_audit_async_sealing.sql`, `0195_auth_invalidations.sql`, `0196_automation_messages.sql` and `0197_automation_approval_allowances.sql`. Keep the existing backup, retained-release and configuration readback procedure until the new image is serving.
- `0173_seeded_github_schedules_off.sql` switches off the schedules of the seeded **Triage GitHub issues** and **Review GitHub pull requests** automations (`github-triage-issues` and `github-review-pull-requests`) that provisioning bound, that are still on and that never fired: a schedule carries no `owner` or `repo`, so they could not start a run. A schedule that ran keeps its state. To use one, name the repository in the trigger's [fixed input](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/automations/triggers#fixed-input) on the automation's **General** tab and turn it on again.
- `0194_audit_async_sealing.sql`: an audited write stores its audit-log entry unsealed, and the worker seals it within seconds. The chain's order is now the order entries are sealed in; entries sealed before the upgrade keep theirs.
- `0195_auth_invalidations.sql` backs the per-process cache of sessions and memberships, `AUTH_REQUEST_CACHE`, on by default: a sign-out, a password change, a revoked passkey, a role change or a removal reaches every API process within about a second. Set it to `off` to read the database on every request. With more than a few API replicas, route each user's requests to the same replica (sticky sessions on the session cookie): every replica has its own cache. See the [environment reference](https://docs.tale.dev/self-hosted/configuration/environment-reference).
- `AUTOMATION_RUNNER_PROCESSES` (`1`–`16`) sets how many processes a backend replica evaluates automation code in: unset, `2` on `backend-api` and, on `backend-worker`, one per CPU core but one, at most `4`. Each costs about 75 MB while it runs; lower it on a replica short of memory.
- A rate limit, an unreachable or busy service, or an embedding provider's own failure neither counts toward a schedule's automatic pause nor resets the count ([#4742](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4742), [#4756](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4756)).
- The API contract moves from `3.27.0` to `3.35.0`.
- Known limitation: re-running the Release workflows of v0.5.78–v0.5.80 moved the `:latest` images back to older releases on 2026-10-10: to v0.5.80 at 09:17 UTC, to v0.5.78 at 09:22 UTC and to v0.5.79 at 09:55 UTC, until this release's images replaced them on 2026-10-11 ([#4740](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4740)). A deployment that pulled `latest` in that window, such as `compose.yml` without `VERSION`, ran older code against a forward-only schema that newer migrations may already have changed. Set `VERSION` to the release you deploy, such as `0.5.83`, and upgrade.
